positioning: Box Core combines constrained local intent, Git-compatible desired state, deterministic approval, reproducible NixOS activation, Home Assistant physical integration, hardware evidence and recovery for owner-controlled edge systems.

neighbours.name: SelfPrivacy Catalog
boxCoreDistinction: private AI and complete edge node
separate configuration, secret and data planes
neighbours.complementarity: Reuse compatible service definitions rather than rebuilding a generic catalogue.

neighbours.name: NixOS Agent-Based Deployment Stack
boxCoreDistinction: one or a small number of owner-controlled systems
no support-plane access to customer content
neighbours.complementarity: Use nix-fleet as an optional transport when central fleet management is required.

neighbours.name: NixEdgeOpt
boxCoreDistinction: human administrative intent to an inspectable diff
no placement optimiser in initial scope
neighbours.complementarity: Delegate future placement optimisation after Box Core approves desired state.

neighbours.name: End-to-end NixOS boot security
neighbours.complementarity: Consume compatible verified-boot work instead of reimplementing signing research.

neighbours.name: Nocloud
boxCoreDistinction: operating and management substrate rather than a file application
neighbours.complementarity: Package compatible storage services on top of Box Core.

neighbours.name: bewCloud
boxCoreDistinction: reproducible node control plane rather than groupware
neighbours.complementarity: Run lightweight user applications as managed services.

neighbours.name: Magic Nix VFS
neighbours.complementarity: Use lazy Nix-store distribution as an optional artefact delivery mechanism.

remainingWeaknesses: The end-to-end Voice-to-GitOps runtime is not public.
No hardware profile has public validation evidence.
The proposal is broader than several neighbouring component projects.
The integration can look like assembly unless policy and recovery contracts are technically strong.
